items.stem: A quadrilateral has diagonals perpendicular and exactly one line of symmetry, but not 4 equal sides. Which quadrilateral is it?
items.markingKey: Only a kite has all these properties. [1]

items.stem: Tomás says: "Every parallelogram has a line of symmetry." Is Tomás correct? Give a reason.
items.answer: No. A general parallelogram (not a rhombus or rectangle) has no lines of symmetry.
items.markingKey: B1 decision; B1 reason or counter-example. [2]

items.stem: Sofia says: "Every rhombus is a square." Is Sofia correct? Give a reason.
items.answer: No. A rhombus need not have right angles, e.g. one with angles 60° and 120°.
items.markingKey: B1 decision; B1 reason or counter-example. [2]

items.markingKey: Co-interior angles between the parallel sides add to 180° (M1); 110° (A1).

items.stem: Explain why a square is a special type of rectangle.
items.answer: A rectangle has four right angles and opposite sides equal; a square has these properties and also all four sides equal.

items.stem: Priya says: "Every rectangle is a parallelogram." Is Priya correct? Give a reason.

items.stem: Explain why a cylinder has infinitely many planes of symmetry.
items.answer: Any vertical plane through the central axis cuts it into two mirror-image halves, and there are infinitely many such planes (plus the horizontal one).
items.markingKey: B1 identifies the planes; B1 explains why others do not work / why the count is as given. [2]

items.stem: A right prism or pyramid has a regular polygon as its base. Work out the number of planes of symmetry of a regular square prism, and explain your answer.
items.markingKey: Each of the 4 lines of symmetry of the regular square base gives a vertical plane (M1) plus one horizontal plane half way up the prism; total 5 (A1).

items.stem: A cuboid measures 4 cm by 4 cm by 12 cm. (a) How many planes of symmetry does it have? (b) A second cuboid has all edges equal to 4 cm. How many planes of symmetry does it have? (c) Explain why your answer to the number of planes depends on whether two edges are equal.
items.answer: (a) 5 (b) 9 (c) Equal edges give square faces, which add diagonal planes of symmetry.

items.stem: What is a plane of symmetry?
options: A flat surface that cuts a solid into two mirror-image halves
A line that cuts a 2D shape in half
items.answer: A flat surface that cuts a solid into two mirror-image halves

items.stem: Explain why a square-based pyramid has 4 planes of symmetry, not 5.
items.answer: The vertical planes through the apex match the 4 lines of symmetry of the square base; there is no horizontal plane because the top and bottom are different.
items.markingKey: B1 identifies the planes; B1 explains why others do not work / why the count is as given. [2]

items.stem: Explain the difference between a line of symmetry and a plane of symmetry, using a rectangle and a cuboid as examples.
items.answer: A line of symmetry divides a 2D shape into two mirror-image halves; a plane of symmetry is a flat surface that divides a 3D solid into two mirror-image halves.
items.markingKey: B1 line for 2D; B1 plane for 3D with examples. [2]

items.stem: A right prism or pyramid has a regular polygon as its base. Work out the number of planes of symmetry of a regular triangular prism, and explain your answer.

items.stem: A right prism or pyramid has a regular polygon as its base. Work out the number of planes of symmetry of a regular hexagonal prism, and explain your answer.
